title: Company update — week 3
text:
**Small charges nobody recognizes.** Since Monday, some customers have seen small card charges they do not recognize, mostly between $0.50 and $5. Screenshots are on X and Reddit; one post with many shares says "Cobalt got hacked".

Known: the charges are real; the security team is investigating with the card processor.
Not known: how many customers; what caused it; whether customer data was exposed.

experience.text: A $4.50 payment on your Cobalt business card shows up twice; you only paid once and do not know why. A market customer asked you whether paying on your Cobalt card reader is safe.
Your own recent Cobalt card payments are all ones you made: none of the unrecognized charges is on your card.

title: Company update — week 4
text: The card processor confirmed a fault that charged some payments twice on November 16 and 17. Separately, a small number of cards were used for test charges of $0.50 to $2 by fraudsters, a common pattern after card numbers are stolen elsewhere, for example on a fake shopping site. Cobalt's own systems were not breached. About 9,000 customers were affected in total.

title: Government shutdown
text:
**Government shutdown.** Overnight, Congress missed its funding deadline, and parts of the federal government shut down. Some federal workers have been sent home; others, such as air traffic controllers and TSA officers, must keep working without pay. Nobody knows how long it will last.

Known: Social Security payments and the Postal Service continue.
Not known: how long it will last; when federal workers will be paid; which services will slow down.

Some of Cobalt's paycheck customers work for the federal government or its contractors. Their next federal paycheck is due on December 30.

pay_paused.text: No pay landed in your Cobalt account this week: your contractor's federal jobs are still paused by the shutdown, so there was no paycheck.

experience.text: Your employer, a contractor, told the crew that its federal building jobs are paused for the shutdown. You are sent home from those jobs without pay until it ends, and nobody can say when that will be.

title: Government shutdown — update
text: The Senate passed a short-term funding bill; the House plans to vote after Christmas. Federal workers have been told they will get back pay once the government reopens. Their December 30 paycheck may be missed.
